title: Free instrument offsets remove 93 percent of curvature information from 20 published Kepler-1658 transit times
abstract: We test a quadratic fit to 20 transit times from the 2022 Kepler-1658 table. A shared-offset fit gives a period derivative of -130.96 +/- 18.74 milliseconds per year. Free WIRC and TESS offsets give -147.38 +/- 72.68 milliseconds per year. Under independent Gaussian errors, these offsets remove 93.36 percent of curvature information. Asymmetric-error fits give similar results. Removing either WIRC visit gives -28.96 +/- 112.65 milliseconds per year in the free-offset model. A constant-period fit needs offsets of about 11 to 12 minutes. Thus the test does not show that small clock errors caused the known signal. Later independent spectroscopy supports a binary and light travel-time explanation; we do not re-test that solution. We report a sensitivity limit for the historic table, with no new object or instrument-cause claim. Code, input rows, source hashes, fit tables, checks and an offline recipe are included.
